Alabama.agency: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA) Driver License Division
Alabama.permitTest: Written knowledge exam based on the Alabama Driver Manual plus an eye exam ($5 exam fee), administered by ALEA.
Alabama.permitDocuments: Certified birth certificate (identity), Social Security card, proof of Alabama residency, and a School Enrollment Form for applicants under 19; Stage I (learner) license fee is $36.25, payable in cash or money order (ALEA does not accept checks).
Alabama.driversEd: Not strictly required: teens either complete a State Department of Education-approved driver education course or submit an ALEA verification form, signed by a parent, guardian or instructor, certifying 50 hours of behind-the-wheel practice.
Alabama.supervisedHours: 50 hours behind-the-wheel practice certified on ALEA's verification form if the teen does not complete an approved driver education course; no night-hour requirement stated
Alabama.licenseMinAge: 16 (Stage II restricted license); Stage III unrestricted at 17 after 6 months in Stage II, or at 18
Alabama.roadTest: Road skills exam given by ALEA at driver license testing sites (online appointments up to two weeks ahead at select locations, walk-ins accepted at all sites); requires parent/grandparent/guardian permission and the $36.25 Stage II fee.
Alabama.restrictions: Stage II: no driving midnight to 6 a.m. (exceptions for parent/guardian, school, religious or work events, emergencies), no more than one passenger besides parents/guardians/family, and no handheld communication devices.

Alaska.permitTest: Written knowledge test (can be taken online at home) and a vision test.
Alaska.permitDocuments: Completed application (Form D1), parental consent (Form 433, or signed in person) with proof of relationship, one primary identity/lawful presence document (e.g., birth certificate or passport), one proof of Alaska residential address, Social Security number, and the $15 fee.
Alaska.supervisedHours: 40 hours total, including at least 10 hours in inclement weather or darkness, certified by a parent on Form 433
Alaska.roadTest: Road test required; scheduled online with DMV or through an approved DMV business partner, then the provisional license is issued at a DMV office or business partner. Applicant must have no traffic convictions or suspensions in the prior 6 months.
Alaska.restrictions: Provisional license: no driving between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m., and no passengers under 21 other than siblings unless accompanied by a licensed driver 21 or older (work-related driving exempt); provisional status lasts at least 6 months and until 18 unless removed with parental permission after 6 months.

Arizona.agency: Arizona Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Division (ADOT MVD)
Arizona.permitTest: Non-commercial knowledge test (in an MVD office or via Permit Test @ Home) plus an in-office vision test.
Arizona.permitDocuments: Original identity and supporting documents per MVD form 40-5144, with parent/guardian signing approval in person (or a notarized application, form 40-5122).
Arizona.driversEd: Optional. Teens can log 30 supervised hours (10 at night) and take the road test; complete approved driver education plus 20 supervised hours (6 at night) and take the road test; or complete a high school or private driver education program, which waives the road test.
Arizona.supervisedHours: 30 hours including 10 at night (or 20 hours including 6 at night with an approved driver education program); none required if an approved driver education program is completed
Arizona.roadTest: Road test taken at an MVD office with an examiner, scheduled through AZMVDNow; bring ID, a vehicle with valid registration and insurance, and a parent/guardian if under 18 (waived for teens who complete an approved driver education program).
Arizona.restrictions: First 6 months of the Class G license: no driving midnight to 5 a.m. (exceptions for school, religious, work, family emergency, or licensed parent/guardian present), no more than one passenger under 18 except siblings, and no cell phone use.

Arkansas.agency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration (DFA) Office of Driver Services; testing by Arkansas State Police (ASP)
Arkansas.permitTest: Written knowledge test and vision screening administered by the Arkansas State Police (an ASP-90 vision referral form from an Arkansas optometrist is needed if the vision screening is failed).
Arkansas.permitDocuments: Proof of identity (e.g., original birth certificate or U.S. passport) and a parent/guardian who assumes financial responsibility (in person or via a notarized ASP 33 form); proof of Arkansas residency is required if the birth certificate is from certain neighboring states.
Arkansas.permitHoldingPeriod: At least 6 months, with no serious accidents or violations in the 6 months before applying for the intermediate license.
Arkansas.supervisedHours: Arkansas does not set a minimum number of supervised practice hours.
Arkansas.roadTest: Driving skills test administered by the Arkansas State Police, scheduled at telegov.egov.com/aspdlskills; testing is offered in all counties.
Arkansas.restrictions: Intermediate license: no driving 11 p.m. to 4 a.m. unless with a licensed driver 21+ or going to/from school, church, or work or in an emergency, and no more than one unrelated passenger under 21 unless a licensed driver 21+ is in the front seat; no cell phone use.

California.permitTest: Vision exam and a knowledge (law) test based on the California Driver's Handbook (80% to pass, three attempts per application).
California.permitDocuments: Online application (DL 44) signed by a parent/guardian (both if joint custody), proof of identity and California residency, the driver education certificate of completion/enrollment, and the application fee; fingerprint scan and photo at the office.
California.driversEd: Required under 17½: driver education (classroom or online) must be completed, or underway, before the permit, plus at least 6 hours of behind-the-wheel training with a licensed driving school instructor.
California.supervisedHours: 50 hours with a California-licensed driver 25 or older, including 10 hours at night
California.roadTest: Behind-the-wheel drive test with a DMV examiner at a DMV office; bring a licensed driver 25 or older, proof of insurance, and a properly registered vehicle (15-day wait and retest fee after a failure).
California.restrictions: First 12 months of the provisional license: no driving 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. and no passengers under 20 unless accompanied by a parent/guardian or licensed driver 25+ (signed-note exceptions for medical, school, work, or family needs).

Colorado.agency: Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
Colorado.permitTest: Written knowledge test (online at home, in office, or through an approved third-party provider) and an in-office vision exam.
Colorado.permitDocuments: Proof of identity (school IDs not accepted), two proofs of Colorado address (a parent's documents are acceptable), an Affidavit of Liability (DR 2460) signed by a licensed adult 21+, the driver education completion certificate, written test confirmation, and fees; fingerprints and photo taken in office.
Colorado.driversEd: Under current rules: ages 15 to 15 1/2 need a 30-hour driver education course; ages 15 1/2 to 16 need the 30-hour course or a 4-hour driver awareness program; ages 16-17 have no course requirement. Applicants under 16 1/2 at licensing also need 6 hours of behind-the-wheel training with an approved instructor (or 12 extra supervised hours if no school is within 30 miles). Starting January 1, 2027, all permit applicants ages 15-17 must complete a 30-hour course, which may be online.
Colorado.supervisedHours: 50 hours including 10 at night, logged on DR 2324 or the RoadReady app
Colorado.roadTest: Drive test taken only with an approved third-party testing school (the DMV cannot book these appointments); retests cost $15.40.
Colorado.restrictions: First year of the minor license: no driving midnight to 5 a.m. (exceptions for parent/guardian, school or work with signed statement, medical emergency); passengers under 21 not allowed for the first 6 months and limited to one for the next 6 months (siblings exempt).

Connecticut.permitTest: Vision test and a 25-question written knowledge test, by appointment at DMV offices.
Connecticut.permitDocuments: Acceptable identification documents, completed Form R-229, parental consent Form 2-D if a parent/guardian is not present, glasses or contacts if used, $40 testing fee (covers vision, knowledge, and road tests), and $19 permit fee.
Connecticut.driversEd: Required: 30 hours of classroom training (including the 8-hour Safe Driving Practices course, with a mandatory 2-hour parent or guardian class) plus 40 hours of behind-the-wheel practice, through a commercial driving school, a high school program, or home training by a qualified trainer.
Connecticut.permitHoldingPeriod: 120 days with commercial or high school training; 180 days with home training
Connecticut.supervisedHours: 40 hours of behind-the-wheel practice (any mix of school, secondary, or parent instruction); no specific night-hour requirement stated
Connecticut.licenseMinAge: 16 years 4 months (practical earliest, after the 120-day hold)
Connecticut.roadTest: Given by the DMV or at an eligible licensed driving school's facility; bring the learner's permit, Form R-229 signed by the trainer, and the EDEC driver education certificate, then take the Road Test Evaluation Report to a DMV office after 48 hours.
Connecticut.restrictions: No driving 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. until 18 (exceptions for work, school, religious activities, medical need); first 6 months passengers limited to parents/guardians and instructors, second 6 months immediate family may also ride.

Delaware.permitTest: Written test and road skills test given through the approved high school/driver education program (or by the DMV in special cases), plus an eye screening at the DMV.
Delaware.permitDocuments: One proof of identity/legal presence showing a parent/guardian's name, proof of SSN, two proofs of Delaware residency (waived if the sponsor is a licensed Delaware driver at the same address), the Delaware Driver Education Certificate (blue/white), the sponsor's signature in front of DMV staff, and the $40 fee.
Delaware.driversEd: Required: an approved driver education course (high school or commercial) must be completed before the Level 1 permit. The state-approved course is 44 hours, including 30 classroom hours.
Delaware.permitHoldingPeriod: 12 months on the Level 1 Learner's Permit (first 6 months fully supervised)
Delaware.supervisedHours: 50 hours including 10 at night, certified by the sponsor after the first 6 months
Delaware.licenseMinAge: 16 years 6 months for unsupervised daytime driving on the Level 1 permit; Class D license at 17 after 12 months on the permit
Delaware.roadTest: The road skills test is part of the driver education program and given by the driver education teacher or the DMV; students needing a specialized evaluation are tested by the DMV.
Delaware.restrictions: After 6 months of the permit: unsupervised driving only 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. (exceptions for church, work, school); throughout the permit year, only the supervisor plus one other passenger (immediate family exempt with supervisor); no cell phone use.

Florida.agency: Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV)
Florida.permitTest: Class E knowledge exam (50 multiple-choice questions, 80% to pass; can be taken online through a third-party administrator if under 18) plus vision and hearing tests at a service center.
Florida.permitDocuments: Signed and notarized Parental Consent Form (71142), proof of DETS course completion, and proof of identity, Social Security number, and residential address (per flhsmv.gov/WhatToBring).
Florida.driversEd: A Driver Education Traffic Safety (DETS) course is required before the learner's license; there is no behind-the-wheel instruction requirement.
Florida.supervisedHours: 50 hours including 10 at night, certified by a parent/guardian/responsible adult 21+ on form 71143
Florida.roadTest: Class E driving skills test taken with a driver license exam provider (FLHSMV/tax collector office) or an approved third-party administrator; the vehicle must have valid registration and insurance and pass the examiner's basic safety inspection.
Florida.restrictions: Age 16: driving only 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; age 17: only 5 a.m. to 1 a.m. (exceptions for driving to/from work or with a licensed driver 21+); no passenger restrictions.

Georgia.permitTest: Knowledge exam (road rules and road signs) and vision exam at a DDS Customer Service Center.
Georgia.permitDocuments: One identity document (e.g., birth certificate or passport), SSN, two proofs of Georgia residency, proof of school enrollment (notarized DDS-1 Certificate of School Enrollment or alternative), a parent/guardian/responsible adult to sign the application, and the $10 permit fee.
Georgia.driversEd: Required at both 16 and 17 under Joshua's Law: 30 hours of classroom or online instruction from a DDS-certified school, plus EITHER 6 hours of behind-the-wheel training with a certified instructor (and 40 supervised hours) OR the parent-taught Parent/Teen Driving Guide (40 hours). The Alcohol and Drug Awareness Program (ADAP/eADAP) is also required.
Georgia.supervisedHours: 40 hours including 6 at night, attested by a parent/guardian at application (no log required)
Georgia.roadTest: Road skills test at a DDS Customer Service Center, booked through DDS road test appointments; bring the driver education completion certificate, ADAP certificate, and proof of school enrollment.
Georgia.restrictions: Class D: no driving midnight to 5 a.m. with no exceptions; first 6 months immediate family passengers only, next 6 months one non-family passenger under 21, then up to three non-family passengers under 21.

Hawaii.agency: Hawaii Department of Transportation (sets statewide rules and driver education program); licenses are issued by the county driver licensing offices (e.g., City and County of Honolulu Department of Customer Services)
Hawaii.permitTest: Knowledge test on state and county traffic laws plus an eyesight (vision) test.
Hawaii.permitDocuments: Original or certified proof of legal presence, legal name, and date of birth (a certified birth certificate is required for minors), proof of Hawaii principal residence, and SSN information (Honolulu lists SSN documents as optional); the permit application must be signed by both parents or the certified custodial parent; permit fee is $5.00.
Hawaii.driversEd: Required for applicants 16-17: a state-certified driver education course plus behind-the-wheel training from a DOT-authorized instructor, with completion certificates shown before the road test. HDOT guidance specifies 30 hours of classroom instruction (spread over at least 6 weeks) and 6 hours of behind-the-wheel training; HDOT has allowed classroom instruction in person, virtually, or a combination (2020 guidance).
Hawaii.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, recorded on a notarized practice log through the driver education program.
Hawaii.roadTest: Road examination at a county Driver Licensing Center (Oahu offers online appointments; tests run Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m.-3:30 p.m.); bring a current, unexpired instruction permit and driver ed/behind-the-wheel completion certificates; road test fee is $8.00 and scores are valid 30 days.
Hawaii.restrictions: No driving 11 p.m.-5 a.m. unless a licensed parent or guardian is in the front seat (exceptions for work or school-authorized activities with a signed statement), and no more than one passenger under 18 who is not a household member unless a licensed parent or guardian is present.

Idaho.agency: Idaho Transportation Department (ITD), Division of Motor Vehicles; licenses issued at county driver's license offices
Idaho.permitTest: Vision test is required for the driver training permit; the written knowledge test is taken later before licensing (or before a Class D instruction permit for applicants 17 and older).
Idaho.permitDocuments: Certified birth certificate, acceptable photo ID, Social Security card or number, proof of Idaho residency, a liability signer (birth parent or court-ordered guardian) for applicants under 18, a school Verification of Compliance (VOC) or proof of graduation for applicants under 18, and lawful presence documents if applicable; driver training permit fee is $21.50.
Idaho.driversEd: Required for all applicants under 17: 30 hours of classroom instruction, 6 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction, and 6 hours of in-car observation with a licensed instructor (public school courses have a 30-day minimum). Online classroom is available through the Idaho Digital Learning Alliance course, which is required for the Parent-Student On-Road Driver Training option in districts without a program.
Idaho.permitHoldingPeriod: 6 calendar months of supervised driving on the Supervised Instruction Permit (after driver ed is passed)
Idaho.roadTest: Written knowledge test at the county driver's license office and a road skills test by appointment with an approved third-party skills tester (list available from county offices and the ITD website); skills test fee is $35, and a parent or guardian must sign the GDL Requirements Verification certifying the 50 hours.
Idaho.restrictions: Licensees under 16 may drive only during daylight hours unless accompanied by a licensed driver 21 or older in the front seat; licensees under 17 may carry no more than one passenger under 17 (relatives excepted) during the first 6 months.

Illinois.agency: Illinois Secretary of State (ILSOS), Driver Services Department
Illinois.permitMinAge: 15 (must be enrolled in an approved driver education course)
Illinois.permitTest: Vision test and written knowledge test.
Illinois.permitDocuments: Proof of date of birth, proof of residency, and an instructor-signed application or official letter on school letterhead showing driver ed enrollment, with parent or legal guardian consent; standard SOS identity and SSN documentation also applies.
Illinois.driversEd: Required for applicants under 18: a state-approved course of at least 30 hours of classroom training and 6 hours of behind-the-wheel training.
Illinois.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, supervised by a parent or licensed adult 21 or older (parent or guardian certifies on the 50-hour log)
Illinois.roadTest: Driving test at a Secretary of State driver services facility, or taken during the driver education course: students who complete an accredited high school course with a combined A or B may not need a facility test. A parent or guardian must accompany the teen to consent or provide a notarized Affidavit/Consent for Minor to Drive.
Illinois.restrictions: No driving 10 p.m.-6 a.m. Sunday-Thursday or 11 p.m.-6 a.m. Friday-Saturday (local curfews may differ); for the first 12 months or until 18, no more than one passenger under 20 except siblings, stepsiblings, children, or stepchildren.

Indiana.permitMinAge: 15 if enrolled in an approved driver education course; 16 without driver education
Indiana.permitTest: Vision screening and a knowledge exam (no appointment needed unless the exam must be read aloud).
Indiana.permitDocuments: Documents proving identity, Social Security number, lawful status, and Indiana residency (two documents, or an Indiana Residency Affidavit signed by an adult household member).
Indiana.driversEd: Not mandatory, but it shortens the wait to license. Approved programs have 30 hours of classroom instruction (online is allowed as an alternative) plus 6 hours of behind-the-wheel training with a BMV-licensed school.
Indiana.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, logged on the Log of Supervised Driving (required even after driver education)
Indiana.licenseMinAge: 16 with completed driver education; 16 years 270 days without driver education
Indiana.roadTest: Driving skills test with the behind-the-wheel driver ed provider under the skills test waiver program, or at a BMV branch when applying (branch testing is required if the student scored 79% or below in driver ed or the provider cannot test); bring the signed supervised driving log.
Indiana.restrictions: First 180 days: no driving 10 p.m.-5 a.m. and no passengers unless a qualifying adult is in the front seat (own child, sibling, or spouse excepted); after 180 days and until 18: no driving after 11 p.m. Sunday-Thursday, 1-5 a.m. Saturday-Sunday, or before 5 a.m. Monday-Friday, with exceptions for work, school, and religious activities.

Iowa.agency: Iowa Department of Transportation (Iowa DOT), Motor Vehicle Division
Iowa.permitTest: Knowledge and vision tests; the knowledge test can be taken at a DMV or county treasurer office, at home with a parent proctor, or at participating schools.
Iowa.permitDocuments: A primary form of identification, proof of residency, and proof of Social Security number, plus written parent or guardian consent (in person or on Parent's/Guardian's Written Consent Form 430018).
Iowa.driversEd: Required for the intermediate license: an Iowa-approved course with at least 30 hours of classroom instruction and 6 hours of in-car instruction (at least 3 on streets or highways). Parent-taught driver education is also an option.
Iowa.supervisedHours: 20 hours, including 2 at night, certified by affidavit for the intermediate license (another 10 hours, 2 at night, are required later for the full license)
Iowa.roadTest: The drive test is usually handled through the driver education program; a DMV drive test is required if the driver ed instructor requests it or if the teen completed Parent-Taught Driver Education.
Iowa.restrictions: No unsupervised driving 12:30 a.m.-5 a.m. (a parent can sign a waiver for school activities and work), and for the first 6 months no more than one unrelated minor passenger unless a parent or guardian waives this at issuance; passengers are limited to the number of seat belts.

Kansas.agency: Kansas Department of Revenue, Division of Vehicles (Driver's License Bureau)
Kansas.permitTest: Vision and written tests, or a driver education certificate of completion in place of the written test.
Kansas.permitDocuments: One lawful presence/identity document (e.g., state-issued birth certificate or passport), SSN proof (Social Security card, W-2/1099, or pay stub with the full number), and two proofs of Kansas residential address, plus parental approval for applicants 14-15; book through the KDOR appointment system.
Kansas.driversEd: Required only for the restricted license at 15; not required for the instruction permit or for licensing at 16 and older.
Kansas.permitHoldingPeriod: 1 year (for applicants 14-16 moving to a restricted license); driver ed permit (DE-99) time does not count
Kansas.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, certified by a parent or guardian affidavit; at least 25 hours are required for the restricted license at 15, and the full 50 must be submitted before 16 to move to less restricted privileges
Kansas.licenseMinAge: 15 (restricted license, driver ed required); 16 for less restricted privileges
Kansas.roadTest: Vision, written, and driving tests at a Division of Vehicles driver's license office by appointment, or a driver education certificate of completion in lieu of the written and driving tests.
Kansas.restrictions: At 15, driving is limited to travel to and from work, school, and religious activities (or anytime with a licensed adult 21+), with no non-sibling minor passengers; at 16, driving is allowed 5 a.m.-9 p.m. plus work, school, and religious trips at any time, with no more than one non-sibling passenger under 18, until 6 months have passed or age 17.

Kentucky.agency: Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC), Division of Driver Licensing; knowledge and skills tests are given by Kentucky State Police (KSP)
Kentucky.permitTest: Written knowledge and vision tests administered by Kentucky State Police (schedule through KSP; bring documents to a KYTC Regional office the same day first).
Kentucky.permitDocuments: Original or certified birth certificate, Social Security card, one proof of Kentucky residency (two for REAL ID), a TC 94-200 KY High School Compliance Verification Form from the school, and a parent or legal guardian listed on the birth certificate to sign the application; permit fee $15 ($18 REAL ID).
Kentucky.driversEd: Required for drivers under 18: a 4-hour approved course, chosen from Alive at 25 (free, in person or Zoom), RightLane Online ($12.50, online), or a participating high school course. Exact timing in the GDL sequence is described differently across KYTC materials.
Kentucky.roadTest: Road skills test by appointment with Kentucky State Police (go straight to KSP on test day); bring the completed and signed Practice Driving Log, a licensed driver 21 or older, and a properly registered and insured vehicle; intermediate license fee is $15 ($18 REAL ID).
Kentucky.restrictions: No driving midnight-6 a.m. except for work, school, or emergencies, and no more than one unrelated passenger under 20 unless supervised by a licensed adult 21 or older.

Louisiana.agency: Louisiana Department of Public Safety, Office of Motor Vehicles (OMV)
Louisiana.permitMinAge: 15 (a Temporary Instructional Permit for driver ed is available at 14)
Louisiana.permitTest: Vision test (20/40 in one eye) and a 40-question knowledge test with a minimum score of 80%, given by OMV or the driving school.
Louisiana.permitDocuments: Certified birth certificate, SSN verification, proof of address, and the driver education Certificate of Successful Completion (surrendered with the TIP), with a custodial parent or legal guardian present to sign (guardians bring guardianship papers); photocopies are not accepted; basic license fee is $32.25 plus up to a $6 service fee.
Louisiana.driversEd: Required: a 38-hour driver education course must be completed before the learner's permit. Classroom can start in 8th grade within 90 days of the 15th birthday; behind-the-wheel training starts at 15 on a Temporary Instructional Permit.
Louisiana.permitHoldingPeriod: 180 days (and until age 16 for permits issued at 15)
Louisiana.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 15 at night, attested by a parent or legal guardian
Louisiana.roadTest: Road skills test administered by the driver education provider or driving school (the OMV permits page says all road skills tests must be performed at a driving school; the GDL fact sheet says 'OMV or driving school').
Louisiana.restrictions: No driving 11 p.m.-5 a.m. unless with a licensed parent/guardian, adult 21+, or sibling 18+, and between 6 p.m. and 5 a.m. no more than one passenger under 21 who is not immediate family unless a licensed adult 21+ is present.

Maine.agency: Maine Department of the Secretary of State, Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV)
Maine.permitTest: Written driving exam scheduled by the BMV after the application is processed, plus a free vision screening at the exam (or an eye exam form from a doctor).
Maine.permitDocuments: Learner's Permit application form, $35 fee, two forms of identification, proof of Maine residency, a driver education completion certificate (applicants under 18), and a birth certificate (applicants under 23); the SSN must be on file or provided, and a parent or guardian must accompany applicants under 18 to sign the license application.
Maine.driversEd: Required for applicants under 18, and must be completed before applying for the learner's permit (the course certificate is part of the permit application).
Maine.supervisedHours: 70 hours, including 10 at night, logged after the permit is issued, with a supervising driver at least 20 years old who has held a license at least 2 years
Maine.roadTest: Road test given by BMV examiners after 6 months on the permit; a parent or guardian certifies the 70-hour practice log (form MVE-21).
Maine.restrictions: For 270 days, the intermediate license bars driving midnight-5 a.m. and carrying any passengers other than immediate family members unless accompanied by a qualified licensed operator; cell phone use is also prohibited.

Maryland.agency: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA)
Maryland.permitTest: Vision screening and a knowledge test at a full-service MVA office appointment.
Maryland.permitDocuments: Proof of identity (birth certificate, U.S. passport, or similar; dependents whose document lacks a parent's name also need proof of parental relationship), proof of Social Security number, and for applicants under 16 a school attendance form (DL-300 in a sealed envelope from the school, or DL-300A co-signed by a parent/guardian); appointment booked through myMVA.
Maryland.driversEd: Required: a Maryland-certified driver education course with 30 hours of classroom instruction and 6 hours of behind-the-wheel training (behind-the-wheel starts after the permit is issued).
Maryland.permitHoldingPeriod: 9 months (restarts if convicted of or given probation before judgment for a moving violation)
Maryland.supervisedHours: 60 hours, including 10 at night, with a supervising driver 21 or older who has held a license at least 3 years
Maryland.roadTest: Behind-the-wheel test by required appointment at an MVA branch office; bring a valid learner's permit, vehicle registration, proof of insurance, the signed practice skills log, driver ed completion verification, and a licensed supervising driver.
Maryland.restrictions: Drivers under 18 may not drive midnight-5 a.m. unless accompanied by a licensed driver 21+ with 3 years' experience or traveling to or from work, school, volunteer, or athletic activities, and for the first 151 days may not carry passengers under 18 other than immediate family without a qualified supervising driver.

Massachusetts.agency: Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV), MassDOT
Massachusetts.permitTest: 25-question knowledge exam (18 correct to pass) on rules of the road, OUI consequences, and the Junior Operator Law, which can be taken online with a webcam, plus an in-person vision screening (field of vision and basic colors).
Massachusetts.permitDocuments: Start the application online, then bring identity documents (per the RMV ID requirements list), the completed application, and the $30 permit fee to an RMV Service Center (or AAA for members); a parent or guardian must sign the application for applicants under 18.
Massachusetts.driversEd: Required for applicants under 18: 30 hours of classroom instruction, 12 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction and 6 hours observing another student's lesson, plus a 2-hour parent or guardian class (unless the parent took one in the past 5 years).
Massachusetts.permitHoldingPeriod: 6 consecutive months, with a clean driving record for 6 months before the road test (a suspension restarts the count)
Massachusetts.supervisedHours: 40 hours certified by a parent or guardian (reduced to 30 hours if the teen completes an approved driver skills development program); no separate night-hour minimum is stated
Massachusetts.roadTest: Scheduled with the RMV and taken with an RMV examiner; the teen must bring a sponsor who is at least 21, has at least 1 year of driving experience, and holds a valid license.
Massachusetts.restrictions: No driving 12:30 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. unless accompanied by a parent or guardian, and for the first 6 months no passengers under 18 other than siblings (restrictions apply until 18).

Michigan.agency: Michigan Department of State (Secretary of State)
Michigan.permitMinAge: 14 years 9 months (Level 1 Learner's License; Segment 1 enrollment at 14 years 8 months)
Michigan.permitTest: Vision test at a Secretary of State office; knowledge instruction and testing are part of Segment 1 driver education rather than a separate state knowledge test.
Michigan.permitDocuments: Segment 1 Certificate of Completion, proof of Social Security number, citizenship or legal presence, identity, and two Michigan residency documents (originals or certified copies), with a parent or guardian present to sign.
Michigan.driversEd: Required. Segment 1: at least 24 hours of classroom and 6 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction plus 4 hours of observation, over at least 3 weeks. Segment 2: at least 6 hours of classroom (max 2 hours per day), taken after 3 months on the Level 1 license and 30 logged supervised hours (2 at night). Online-only courses and parent-taught or home-school courses are not accepted.
Michigan.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including at least 10 at night (30 hours, including 2 at night, must be logged before Segment 2)
Michigan.roadTest: Taken through independent driver testing businesses approved by the Secretary of State (fees set by the business); it includes a vehicle inspection, a basic control skills test, and an on-road test, and the teen must be at least 15 and accompanied by a parent or guardian with no violations or at-fault crashes in the prior 90 days.
Michigan.restrictions: Level 2: no driving 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. and no more than one passenger under 21 (immediate family excepted), unless accompanied by a parent/guardian or licensed adult 21+ or driving to/from work or an authorized activity.

Minnesota.agency: Minnesota Department of Public Safety, Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS)
Minnesota.permitTest: Written knowledge test (online at home with a proctor or at a DVS exam station by appointment) and a vision test.
Minnesota.permitDocuments: Completed application, fee, and parent or guardian signature and certification, plus proof that the classroom phase of driver education is done and behind-the-wheel training is underway.
Minnesota.driversEd: Required for applicants under 18: 30 hours of classroom instruction (in person or online), or 15 hours in a program that runs classroom and behind-the-wheel together, before the permit; 6 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction must be completed before the provisional license.
Minnesota.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 15 at night (40 hours, still including 15 at night, if a parent or guardian completes the 90-minute supplemental parent class), logged and signed by a parent or guardian
Minnesota.roadTest: Skills (road) test taken at a DVS exam station; bring the application, fee, signed supervised driving log, driver education completion (white) card, parental approval, and the parent class certificate if claiming the 40-hour option.
Minnesota.restrictions: First 6 months: no driving midnight to 5 a.m. (exceptions for work, school events, or with a licensed driver 25+) and only one passenger under 20; months 7-12: up to three passengers under 20 (immediate family and parent/guardian-accompanied trips excepted).

Mississippi.agency: Mississippi Department of Public Safety, Driver Service Bureau
Mississippi.permitTest: Knowledge exam (must be taken in person) and an eye exam.
Mississippi.permitDocuments: Signed application, original birth certificate (no photocopies), Social Security card or document showing all 9 digits, two proofs of residency, and a current School Attendance Form (ages 15-17); fee $7 for a 2-year permit.
Mississippi.driversEd: Not required for the regular license; completion of a certified driver education course is required only for the hardship license (ages 15-17).
Mississippi.permitHoldingPeriod: 12 months, or until the 17th birthday, whichever comes first (applicants 17+ may get the permit and license the same day)
Mississippi.supervisedHours: No minimum is set in law, but the parent or guardian affidavit that replaces the road test certifies that the teen has driven at least 50 hours.
Mississippi.roadTest: No road test is required: a parent or guardian signs a Waiver of Road Testing Affidavit, and the teen brings it with the valid permit and an up-to-date School Attendance Form (valid 30 days) to a Driver Service Bureau office.
Mississippi.restrictions: Intermediate license: no unsupervised driving 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday-Thursday or 11:30 p.m. to 6 a.m. Friday-Saturday (except to or from work, or with a licensed driver 21+); no passenger restriction.

Missouri.agency: Missouri Department of Revenue, Driver License Bureau (testing by the Missouri State Highway Patrol)
Missouri.permitTest: Vision, road sign recognition, and written knowledge tests at a Missouri State Highway Patrol driver examination station.
Missouri.permitDocuments: Proof of identity, lawful status, Social Security number, and Missouri residency, with a qualified person (parent, guardian, etc.) present at the license office to sign a permission statement.
Missouri.driversEd: Not required; a qualified driving instructor may provide some of the 40 supervised hours.
Missouri.permitHoldingPeriod: 182 days (counted from the day after issuance), with no traffic convictions in the prior 6 months and no alcohol offenses in the prior 12 months
Missouri.supervisedHours: 40 hours, including at least 10 at night (sunset to sunrise), with a qualified person, grandparent, or qualified driving instructor, verified at the license office
Missouri.roadTest: Driving test taken at a Missouri State Highway Patrol driver examination station (written, sign, and vision tests repeated only if older than one year).
Missouri.restrictions: No driving alone 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. (except school activities, work, emergencies, or with a licensed driver 21+); first 6 months no more than one non-family passenger under 19, then no more than three.

Montana.agency: Montana Department of Justice, Motor Vehicle Division (MVD)
Montana.permitMinAge: 14 years 6 months (traffic education learner permit, issued by the instructor to students in a state-approved course); 15 (learner license at an MVD exam station without traffic education)
Montana.permitTest: Written knowledge test based on the Montana Driver's Manual.
Montana.permitDocuments: Parental consent, proof of identity, proof of residency, proof of authorized presence, and fees; the applicant must know (but need not show proof of) their Social Security number.
Montana.driversEd: State law (MCA 61-5-132) requires applicants under 18 to complete either a traditional OPI-approved traffic education course (at least 60 hours of instruction, including 6 hours behind the wheel in traffic, over at least 25 days) or a Department of Justice-approved alternative traffic education course.
Montana.permitHoldingPeriod: 6 months plus 1 day, with no traffic, alcohol, or drug violations during that time
Montana.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, after a traditional course (75 hours, including 15 at night, after a DOJ-approved alternative course), logged by a parent, guardian, or responsible adult (Teen Driving Log or RoadReady app)
Montana.licenseMinAge: 15 (First-Year Restricted License; statutory minimum licensing age is 15)
Montana.roadTest: Regular drive test scheduled at an MVD driver license station; bring identity, residency, and authorized-presence documents, the driving log, the valid permit, the signed Parent/Legal Guardian Certification (form 21-1600), and registration and insurance for the test vehicle.
Montana.restrictions: For the first year: no driving 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. (exceptions for emergencies, farm work, school, church, work, or parent-authorized trips); first 6 months only one unrelated passenger under 18, second 6 months up to three, unless supervised by a licensed driver 18+.

Nebraska.permitMinAge: 15 (Learner's Permit, LPD; may apply 60 days early)
Nebraska.permitDocuments: Proof of U.S. citizenship or lawful status and identity, two proofs of Nebraska address, and a Social Security number that can be verified; LPD fee is $13 ($8 plus $5 security fee).
Nebraska.driversEd: Not strictly required: for the Provisional Operator's Permit, a teen either completes a DMV-approved driver safety course or submits a certification of 50 hours of supervised driving.
Nebraska.permitHoldingPeriod: 6 months (LPE, SCP, or LPD), with fewer than 3 points in that period
Nebraska.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 between sunset and sunrise, certified by a parent, guardian, or licensed driver 21+; not required if the teen completes an approved driver safety course
Nebraska.licenseMinAge: 16 (Provisional Operator's Permit, POP; may apply 60 days early)
Nebraska.roadTest: The written and drive tests are waived for graduates of a DMV-approved driver safety course (the school reports completion electronically and the POP can be obtained online); applicants using the 50-hour form take vision and drive tests at a DMV driver licensing office.
Nebraska.restrictions: No unsupervised driving midnight to 6 a.m. except to or from work or school activities, and for the first 6 months no more than one passenger under 19 who is not immediate family (unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, or licensed driver 21+).

Nevada.permitTest: Written knowledge test (available online) and a vision test (20/40 in at least one eye).
Nevada.permitDocuments: Certification of School Attendance (DMV 301, valid 60 days), proof of identity, Social Security number, two Nevada residency documents, the application (DMV 002), a parent-signed Financial Responsibility Statement and Minor Affidavit (DP-38), and fees ($22.50 license fee plus $25 testing fee).
Nevada.driversEd: Required for most first-time drivers under 18: 30 hours of classroom instruction or an approved online course. If no course is available within 30 miles and the teen has no internet access, 100 hours of supervised driving (10 at night) replace the course. No professional behind-the-wheel hours are listed.
Nevada.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including at least 10 after dark (100 hours, including 10 at night, if driver education is not available), recorded on form DLD-130 or the RoadReady app and signed by a parent or guardian
Nevada.roadTest: Driving skills test scheduled online at a DMV office; bring a parent or guardian, the permit, identity and residency proof, the completed driving log, the application, and a registered, insured vehicle (no rentals).
Nevada.restrictions: No driving 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. except to or from school or work, and for the first 6 months no passengers under 18 except immediate family.

New Hampshire.agency: New Hampshire Department of Safety, Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
New Hampshire.permitMinAge: 15 years 6 months (New Hampshire issues no learner's permit; teens may begin supervised practice at this age)
New Hampshire.permitTest: New Hampshire has no learner's permit. Teens 15½ and older may practice with a parent, guardian or other responsible adult; the knowledge test is taken at licensing, together with the road test.
New Hampshire.permitDocuments: No permit application is needed before supervised practice begins.
New Hampshire.driversEd: Required for all applicants under 18: an approved program with 30 hours of classroom instruction, 10 hours of behind-the-wheel driving and 6 hours of observation with a certified instructor.
New Hampshire.permitHoldingPeriod: No permit to hold; teens practice with a supervising adult from 15½ until they apply for a license at 16.
New Hampshire.supervisedHours: 40 hours, including 10 at night, with a parent, guardian, or other responsible adult, logged on the Driver's Out-of-Class Log Sheet
New Hampshire.roadTest: Vision, knowledge, and road tests are taken at the NH DMV by appointment; bring the application, two proof-of-identity documents, the original green Driver Education Completion Certificate, the Parent/Guardian Authorization Certificate, and the signed out-of-class log sheet.
New Hampshire.restrictions: Under 18: no driving 1 a.m. to 4 a.m., and for the first 6 months no more than one non-family passenger under 25 unless a licensed adult 25+ is present.

New Jersey.permitMinAge: 16 (special learner's permit, through an approved behind-the-wheel driver training course); 17 (examination permit at an MVC Licensing Center without driver training)
New Jersey.permitTest: MVC knowledge test and vision screening (given at the driving school for special learner's permits).
New Jersey.permitDocuments: Permit application (BA-412D for the special learner's permit), 6 points of identification plus proof of Social Security number and New Jersey address under the standard MVC document requirements, and signed parent or guardian consent; the examination permit fee is $10.
New Jersey.driversEd: Required only for the age-16 special learner's permit path: 6 hours of behind-the-wheel training with a licensed instructor in a dual-control vehicle before the permit is validated. The 17-year-old examination permit path has no driver education requirement.
New Jersey.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 during darkness, certified on MVC form BA-CSD (applies to permits issued on or after February 1, 2025, for drivers under 21)
New Jersey.roadTest: Taken with the MVC by appointment (online or at a Licensing Center); after passing, the stamped permit and documents are taken to the road test site (if available) or any Licensing Center for the probationary license, along with the completed BA-CSD form.
New Jersey.restrictions: No driving 11:01 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. (work or religious exemptions with proof), and no more than one passenger besides parents, guardians, or the driver's dependents unless a parent or guardian is present; red GDL decals are required on front and rear plates.

New Mexico.agency: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department, Motor Vehicle Division (MVD)
New Mexico.permitTest: Vision test and MVD knowledge exam; the knowledge exam may be given by an MVD-contracted driver education school.
New Mexico.permitDocuments: Proof of identity and age plus two proofs of New Mexico residency (and a proof of identification number for REAL ID), proof of completion of or current enrollment in a TSB-approved driver education program (referral card), a parent or guardian to sign the application, and a $10 fee.
New Mexico.driversEd: Required. A TSB-approved course with a DWI component: either 30 classroom hours plus 7 one-on-one behind-the-wheel hours (private/approved school) or 56 classroom hours with no behind-the-wheel requirement (public high school program); at least 6 classroom hours cover DWI prevention. Online driver education is not permitted.
New Mexico.permitHoldingPeriod: 6 months (extended 30 days for each qualifying traffic conviction)
New Mexico.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, with a licensed driver 21 or older who has been licensed at least 3 years
New Mexico.roadTest: MVD Road Skills Exam taken at an MVD field office or through an MVD-contracted driver education school; bring the TSB certificate of completion, the signed driving log (50 hours, 10 at night) and, if tested at a school, the MVD Record of Completion, with a parent or guardian to sign.
New Mexico.restrictions: Provisional drivers may not drive from midnight to 5 a.m. without a licensed driver 21 or older (exceptions for school, work, family/medical needs and religious functions), and may carry no more than one passenger under 21 who is not immediate family unless a licensed driver 21 or older is present; provisional license must be held 12 months.

New York.agency: New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
New York.permitTest: Written knowledge (permit) test on the Driver's Manual (traffic laws and road signs); a vision check is also given at the DMV office.
New York.permitDocuments: Application MV-44 with the parental consent section signed by a parent or guardian for applicants under 18, proof of identity and date of birth (e.g., NYS birth certificate or passport), and the Social Security card.
New York.driversEd: Not required. Applicants must instead complete the 5-hour Pre-licensing Course (certificate MV-278) before the road test, unless they complete a state-approved high school or college Driver and Traffic Safety Education course (certificate MV-285), which also allows a senior (Class D) license at 17.
New York.permitHoldingPeriod: 6 months before the road test can be scheduled (applicants under 18)
New York.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including at least 15 after sunset, certified by a parent or guardian on Form MV-262
New York.licenseMinAge: 16 (junior license, Class DJ); earliest in practice is about 16 years 6 months because of the 6-month permit period
New York.roadTest: DMV road test scheduled online (nyrtsscheduler.com) or by phone at a site chosen by ZIP code; bring the learner permit, the original MV-278 or MV-285 certificate and the signed MV-262. The permit fee covers two road tests.
New York.restrictions: Varies by region: upstate, junior drivers may drive unsupervised 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. but 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. only to/from work or school or with a qualifying supervisor; Long Island allows unsupervised driving only for listed purposes (work, school, etc.); junior licensees may not drive in New York City at all; statewide, no more than one passenger under 21 who is not immediate family unless supervised.

North Carolina.agency: North Carolina Department of Transportation, Division of Motor Vehicles (NCDMV)
North Carolina.permitTest: Written, road sign and vision tests at an NCDMV driver license office.
North Carolina.permitDocuments: One document proving identity and date of birth, proof of a Social Security number, one proof of NC residency, the Driver's Education Certificate, and a parent or guardian present (or written consent); the Level 1 permit fee is $25.50.
North Carolina.driversEd: Required: 30 hours of classroom instruction plus at least 6 hours behind the wheel; students may enroll at 14 years 6 months.
North Carolina.supervisedHours: 60 hours, including at least 10 at night; no more than 10 hours per week count toward the total
North Carolina.roadTest: On-the-road test at an NCDMV driver license office or a certified driver education school; bring the Level 1 permit, the printed 60-hour driving log, printed proof of liability insurance, and a vehicle with valid registration (DMV tests require a parent or guardian present); fee is $25.50.
North Carolina.restrictions: Level 2 drivers may drive unsupervised only 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. (plus to/from work or volunteer fire/rescue/EMS duty), with no more than one passenger under 21 who is not a family or household member when unsupervised, and no mobile phone use; Level 3 (full provisional) lifts these after 6 months.

North Dakota.agency: North Dakota Department of Transportation (NDDOT), Driver License Division
North Dakota.permitTest: Rules of the Road knowledge test (in person or online at home) and a vision screening.
North Dakota.permitDocuments: Proof of identity and North Dakota address (per the ID checklist), a Social Security number, and a sponsor's (parent/guardian) signature for applicants under 18; fees are $5 per knowledge test attempt and $15 for the permit.
North Dakota.driversEd: Required for applicants 14-15: an approved formal driver education course of 30 classroom hours plus 6 behind-the-wheel hours and 6 observation hours (or 6 hours at a commercial driving school). Not required for ages 16-17.
North Dakota.permitHoldingPeriod: 12 months for ages 14-15; 6 months for ages 16-17
North Dakota.supervisedHours: 50 hours of practice in varied conditions for teens licensed at 14 or 15; not required for applicants 16 and 17.
North Dakota.licenseMinAge: 15 (restricted Class D license); full license at 16
North Dakota.roadTest: State road test at an NDDOT driver license site, by appointment scheduled online; road test fee is $5.
North Dakota.restrictions: Restricted license holders under 16 may not drive between 9 p.m. (or sunset, if later) and 5 a.m. unless a licensed driver is in the front seat or they are driving directly to/from work, school or religious activities, may drive only vehicles owned by a parent/guardian, and may not use a cell phone; no passenger limit beyond seat belt count.

Ohio.agency: Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV), Ohio Department of Public Safety
Ohio.permitTest: Vision screening and a 40-question multiple-choice knowledge test (75% to pass), taken online or in person at a driver exam station or select deputy registrar.
Ohio.permitDocuments: Proof of full legal name, date of birth, Social Security number (if assigned), Ohio residency, and citizenship or legal presence, plus a parent/guardian (responsible person) with ID to co-sign; buy the permit (TIPIC) within 60 days of passing the test.
Ohio.driversEd: Required: 24 hours of classroom or online instruction plus 8 hours of behind-the-wheel training with a licensed driving school; bring the certificate to the driving test.
Ohio.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including at least 10 at night, logged on Form BMV 5791
Ohio.roadTest: Driving and maneuverability (skills) test at a BMV driver exam station, scheduled through BMV Online Services; bring the permit, the driver education certificate and the signed BMV 5791 log; under-21 applicants who fail wait two days.
Ohio.restrictions: First 12 months: no driving midnight to 6 a.m. (unless with a parent/guardian or for work/school/religious events with documentation) and no more than one non-family passenger unless a parent or guardian is present; after 12 months and until 18, no driving 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. with the same exceptions.

Oklahoma.permitMinAge: 15 (if enrolled and receiving instruction in approved driver education); 16 without driver education
Oklahoma.permitTest: Vision test and a 20-question written exam on Oklahoma traffic laws, road signs and safe driving; the written test may be waived with a driver education completion certificate (not parent-taught).
Oklahoma.permitDocuments: One proof of identity, one proof of lawful presence, one proof of residency (two for REAL ID), your Social Security number, a parent or legal guardian present (or a notarized Parent Authorization form), and the driver education enrollment contract or completion certificate; the permit fee is $42.50.
Oklahoma.driversEd: Required to get a permit at 15 and to test for an intermediate license before 16½; optional at 16 and older. School, commercial and parent-taught courses are accepted.
Oklahoma.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, with a licensed driver at least 21 who has been licensed at least 2 years (Affidavit of Driver Training)
Oklahoma.licenseMinAge: 16 with driver education; 16 years 6 months without
Oklahoma.roadTest: Class D drive test at a Service Oklahoma licensing office or with a designated examiner (certified driver ed instructor); bring the learner permit, proof of insurance, the driver education certificate if applicable, the parent or a notarized Affidavit of Driver Training, the Oklahoma Work Zone Safe course certificate, and a registered vehicle that passes inspection.
Oklahoma.restrictions: Intermediate license holders may drive only 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. unless going to/from school, church or work or with a licensed driver 21+ in front, and may carry only one passenger (or household members only) unless a licensed driver 21+ is in the front seat.

Oregon.agency: Oregon Department of Transportation, Driver and Motor Vehicle Services (DMV)
Oregon.permitTest: 35-question Class C knowledge test ($7 per attempt, online or at a DMV office) and a vision test.
Oregon.permitDocuments: Proof of identity and physical address (more for REAL ID), your Social Security number (or electronic certification that you have none), a parent or legal guardian's signature, and the issuance fee.
Oregon.driversEd: Optional. Passing an ODOT-approved driver education course cuts the required supervised hours from 100 to 50 and can waive the DMV drive test.
Oregon.supervisedHours: 100 hours, or 50 hours with an ODOT-approved driver education course; the supervising driver must be 21 or older and licensed at least 3 years.
Oregon.roadTest: Drive test by appointment with DMV ($45) or a certified Class C third-party testing business; waived if the teen passed an ODOT-approved driver ed course within the past 2 years; bring a registered, insured passenger vehicle and proof of identity/address.
Oregon.restrictions: First 6 months: no passengers under 20 who are not immediate family; second 6 months: no more than three such passengers; throughout, no driving midnight to 5 a.m. except for work, school events or with a licensed driver 25+; restrictions end at 18 or after one year, whichever is first.

Pennsylvania.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT), Driver and Vehicle Services
Pennsylvania.permitTest: Vision screening and an 18-question knowledge test on signs, laws and safe driving (15 correct to pass) at a Driver License Center.
Pennsylvania.permitDocuments: Form DL-180 with the physical exam completed by a health care provider, original proof of identity and date of birth, a signed Social Security card, parent/guardian consent on Form DL-180TD (notarized if they cannot attend), and the applicable fee.
Pennsylvania.driversEd: Not required for the junior license. An approved driver education course is required only for an unrestricted license before 18 (at 17, with 12 months free of crashes and convictions).
Pennsylvania.supervisedHours: 65 hours, including at least 10 at night and 5 in poor weather, certified on Form DL-180C
Pennsylvania.licenseMinAge: 16 (junior license); earliest in practice is about 16 years 6 months because of the 6-month permit period
Pennsylvania.roadTest: Road test at a PennDOT Driver License Center or a PennDOT-certified third-party tester; bring the learner's permit, signed DL-180C, the vehicle's registration card and proof of insurance, and an accompanying licensed adult (originals only).
Pennsylvania.restrictions: Junior license holders may not drive 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. except for work or volunteer service; for the first 6 months no more than one passenger under 18 who is not immediate family unless a parent/guardian is present, rising to three after 6 months (if crash- and conviction-free).

Rhode Island.agency: Rhode Island Division of Motor Vehicles (RI DMV)
Rhode Island.permitTest: Computerized knowledge exam, by appointment (given at the Cranston DMV headquarters for students from non-CCRI driving schools).
Rhode Island.permitDocuments: Application LI-1 signed in person by a parent, legal guardian, licensed foster parent or adult spouse (with ID, and proof of authority for guardians or foster parents), plus the original driver education certificate and proof of identity.
Rhode Island.driversEd: Required: the 33-hour CCRI-certified driver education course before the permit; online courses are not accepted (since July 1, 2022). No behind-the-wheel instructor hours are required by the DMV.
Rhode Island.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, certified by a parent/guardian affidavit
Rhode Island.roadTest: RI DMV road test on a closed course (examiner proctors from outside the vehicle), scheduled online or at a DMV branch; vehicle must have valid RI registration and pass the examiner's equipment check.
Rhode Island.restrictions: Limited provisional drivers may not drive unsupervised 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. (exceptions for work, volunteer fire/rescue/EMS and school athletic activities) and, for the first 12 months, may carry no more than one passenger under 21 who is not family or household.

South Carolina.agency: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV)
South Carolina.permitTest: Vision test and knowledge test at an SCDMV branch (knowledge test must be started before 4 p.m.).
South Carolina.permitDocuments: Government-issued birth certificate, Social Security number, proof of current SC physical address (two for REAL ID), and a qualified adult to sign consent at the branch (or a driver training school representative); fees are $2 for the knowledge test and $2.50 for the permit.
South Carolina.driversEd: Required for teens: 8 hours of classroom instruction and 6 hours of driving, documented on SCDMV Form PDLA from the driver training school or high school.
South Carolina.supervisedHours: 40 hours, including 10 at night, with a qualified licensed driver
South Carolina.licenseMinAge: 15 years 6 months (conditional license); special restricted license at 16
South Carolina.roadTest: Vision and road test at any SCDMV branch (walk-ins 8:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. except a later Wednesday opening; appointments for 2-4 p.m. via public.scscheduler.com); bring Form PDLA certifying school attendance, driver ed and practice hours.
South Carolina.restrictions: Conditional and special restricted drivers may drive alone 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. (8 p.m. during daylight saving time), only with a licensed driver 21+ from then until midnight, and only with a qualified individual from midnight to 6 a.m.; no more than two passengers under 21 unless a licensed adult 21+ is present (family and students going to/from school exempt).

South Dakota.agency: South Dakota Department of Public Safety, Driver Licensing Program
South Dakota.permitTest: Knowledge and vision tests at a driver exam station; the knowledge test is waived with a driver ed certificate from an approved course passed within the last year.
South Dakota.permitDocuments: Certified birth certificate, Social Security card (or approved alternates), two pieces of mail proving residential address (teen's or parent's name), parent/guardian consent in person or by notarized Parental Consent Form, and a $38 fee.
South Dakota.driversEd: Not required. An approved driver ed course shortens the instruction permit holding period (180 days instead of 275), waives the permit knowledge test, and waives the drive test for the Restricted Minor's Permit if passed within the last year.
South Dakota.permitHoldingPeriod: 275 days (180 days after passing driver ed) for permits issued on or after July 1, 2020
South Dakota.supervisedHours: 50 hours of adult-supervised driving, including 10 hours in inclement weather and 10 hours after dark
South Dakota.licenseMinAge: 14 (Restricted Minor's Permit); in practice about 14 years 9 months without driver ed, or 14 years 6 months with driver ed, because of the holding period
South Dakota.roadTest: Drive test taken by appointment at a state driver exam station (book at dps.sd.gov or 605-773-6883), waived if an approved driver ed class was passed within the last year; bring the instruction permit, driver ed certificate (if any), two proofs of address, and the $38 fee.
South Dakota.restrictions: Restricted Minor's Permit holders may drive alone only from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. (with exceptions for direct trips to school, church, work, or farm work), with no non-family passengers for the first 6 months and then no more than one non-family passenger under 18.

Tennessee.agency: Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security, Driver Services Division
Tennessee.permitTest: Written knowledge test (ages 15 to 17 may take it online through e-Services or at a Driver Services Center) plus an in-person vision screening.
Tennessee.permitDocuments: Proof of U.S. citizenship or legal presence, proof of Social Security number, two proofs of Tennessee residency, a school attendance form signed within 30 days by the principal or counselor, and a parent or guardian present to sign the minor affidavit and financial responsibility form (originals or certified copies only).
Tennessee.driversEd: Not required for the GDL; a parent, guardian, or driving instructor certifies 50 practice hours instead.
Tennessee.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, certified on the 50-Hour Certification form
Tennessee.roadTest: Road skills test at a local Driver Services Center, accompanied by a licensed driver 21 or older; online scheduling is available for in-state applicants 16 and older.
Tennessee.restrictions: Intermediate Restricted License holders may not drive from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. and may carry only one passenger (unless accompanied as allowed by law); permit holders may not drive from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.

Texas.agency: Texas Department of Public Safety, Driver License Division
Texas.permitTest: Knowledge exam (taken during the driver ed classroom portion or at the DPS office) plus a vision exam at the DPS office.
Texas.permitDocuments: Completed DL-14B application, proof of U.S. citizenship or lawful presence, Texas residency, and identity, SSN (verified electronically), Texas Driver Education Certificate showing classroom completion (DE-964/DEE-964 or DE-964E), a high school diploma/GED or VOE form, a parent or guardian present (or a notarized signed application), and the application fee.
Texas.driversEd: Required. Before the learner license you must finish 6 classroom hours (concurrent method) or 24 hours (block method). The provisional license requires the behind-the-wheel portion: 7 hours of in-car observation and 7 hours of in-car instruction. Commercial schools, public schools, and parent-taught courses are all accepted. The Impact Texas Teen Driver (ITTD) program must be completed within 90 days before the driving test.
Texas.supervisedHours: 30 hours of behind-the-wheel practice, including 10 at night, with a licensed driver 21 or older
Texas.roadTest: Driving test at a DPS driver license office by online appointment (bring proof of current registration and insurance for the test vehicle), or at a driver education school, which gives DPS the results in a sealed envelope or through the TPST Submission Portal.
Texas.restrictions: Provisional license holders may not drive from midnight to 5 a.m. except for work, school activities, or emergencies, and may carry no more than one non-family passenger under 21.

Utah.agency: Utah Department of Public Safety, Driver License Division
Utah.permitTest: A 50-question closed-book written knowledge test and an eye (vision) test at a Driver License Division office.
Utah.permitDocuments: Proof of identity, lawful presence (non-citizens), Social Security number, and Utah address (per the Required Documents list), plus a parent or guardian co-signer for financial responsibility if under 18; the handbook lists a $19 permit fee.
Utah.driversEd: Required for ages 15 to 18: 6 hours behind the wheel plus classroom of 27 hours (high school), 18 hours (commercial school), or 30 hours (online home study). Utah-approved online courses are accepted, but out-of-state online courses are not. Six observation hours are listed but are not required by state law.
Utah.roadTest: Driving skills test plus a Traffic Safety and Trends Exam, taken at a Driver License Division office by appointment (age 16+), at a high school, or with a DLD-certified third-party tester at a commercial driving school (from age 15, separate fee).
Utah.restrictions: No passengers other than immediate family for the first six months or until 18 (unless a licensed driver 21+ is in the front seat), and 16-year-old license holders may not drive from midnight to 5 a.m. except for work, school activities, agriculture, emergencies, or with a licensed driver 21+.

Vermont.agency: Vermont Agency of Transportation, Department of Motor Vehicles
Vermont.permitTest: A knowledge test taken online through the myDMV portal, based on the Vermont Driver's License Manual.
Vermont.permitDocuments: License/Permit Application (VL-021) signed by a parent or guardian before the test, proof of identity, a clean driving record for the previous two years, and the test fee plus a $24 learner's permit fee.
Vermont.driversEd: Required for the junior license: 30 hours of classroom, 6 hours behind the wheel, and 6 hours of observation; the instructor must log completion in the Driver Education Certification Service before a road test.
Vermont.supervisedHours: 40 hours, including 10 at night, in addition to the 6 behind-the-wheel hours in driver ed, certified by a parent or guardian
Vermont.roadTest: DMV road test scheduled through myDMV. Bring the valid learner's permit, proof of identity and residency, SSN, driver ed completion, a valid insurance card and registration for a clean, inspected test vehicle, and the fees; a parent or guardian signs the application.
Vermont.restrictions: There is no night-driving curfew; for the first 3 months the driver may drive alone or with only a qualifying supervisor (parent/guardian, instructor, or licensed person 25+), family passengers are allowed in months 4 to 6, and passengers are unrestricted after 6 months.

Virginia.permitTest: Vision screening and a two-part knowledge exam taken during the application appointment at a DMV customer service center (remote testing in some schools).
Virginia.permitDocuments: Application DL 1P signed by a parent or guardian, one proof of identity, one proof of legal presence, two proofs of Virginia residency, and SSN if issued (original documents only), plus a $3 permit fee and the yearly license cost.
Virginia.driversEd: Required under 18: 36 classroom periods, 7 driving periods, and 7 observation periods (50 minutes each), plus a final road skills exam. The classroom portion may be taken online through a driver training school. A 90-minute parent/teen component is also required, and must be in person in Planning District 8 (Northern Virginia).
Virginia.supervisedHours: 45 hours, including 15 after sunset, certified by a parent or guardian
Virginia.roadTest: The road skills exam is the final part of the state-approved driver education program. The instructor issues a Driver Training Certificate (DTS B) that serves as a temporary license for 180 days, and the permanent license follows at a juvenile court licensing ceremony or by mail.
Virginia.restrictions: No driving from midnight to 4 a.m. (exceptions for work, supervised school/civic/religious activities, a parent or adult spouse in the front seat, and emergencies); only one non-family passenger under 21 during the first year, and up to three after that only in limited circumstances.

Washington.permitMinAge: 15 (if enrolled in an approved driver training course); 15 years 6 months otherwise
Washington.permitTest: Knowledge test taken in person at an approved testing location (driver training school or testing business); a vision screening is part of the license application.
Washington.permitDocuments: A Washington Driver License number (pre-apply through License Express), proof of identity if you want a photo permit, a parent or guardian present or giving online permission with proof of relationship (such as a birth certificate), and a $35 permit fee.
Washington.driversEd: Required for a license before 18: an approved course of 30 classroom hours and 6 behind-the-wheel hours (the hours appear on DOL's out-of-state equivalency rule). Online self-paced and parent-taught courses are not approved.
Washington.roadTest: Knowledge and drive tests are scheduled at a DOL-approved driver testing location (driver training schools and testing businesses, fees vary), and the license is issued after a vision screening, photo, and parental authorization.
Washington.restrictions: No driving from 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. unless with a licensed driver 25 or older; no passengers under 20 (except immediate family) for the first 6 months and no more than 3 for the next 6 months; restrictions end after one year of clean driving.

West Virginia.agency: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles
West Virginia.permitDocuments: An application signed by a parent, custodial parent or legal guardian, plus identity and residency documents.
West Virginia.driversEd: Not required; a Driver Education Card may be used in place of the 50-hour certification form.
West Virginia.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, certified by a parent or guardian (or replaced by a Driver Education Card)
West Virginia.roadTest: Road skills test ($7.50) taken through the WV DMV after 6 infraction-free months on the Level 1 permit.
West Virginia.restrictions: Driving from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. requires a supervising adult (exceptions for work, school, religious activities, and emergencies); no non-family passengers under 20 for the first six months, then no more than one.

Wisconsin.agency: Wisconsin Department of Transportation, Division of Motor Vehicles (WisDOT DMV)
Wisconsin.permitMinAge: 15 (must be enrolled in a certified driver education program)
Wisconsin.permitTest: Knowledge, highway signs, and vision tests; ages 15 to 17 may take the knowledge test online through Know2Drive for a $10 fee.
Wisconsin.permitDocuments: Completed MV3001 application signed by a driver ed instructor and an adult sponsor, proof of citizenship or legal status, name and date of birth, identity, SSN, and school enrollment (or graduation, equivalency, or home-based education), plus licensing fees.
Wisconsin.driversEd: Required under 18, including classroom and behind-the-wheel instruction; behind-the-wheel and observation hours may be split 6/6, 7/4, 8/2, or 9/0 (driving/observation), and classroom is required only for students under 18.
Wisconsin.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night (30 hours for permits issued before July 11, 2021)
Wisconsin.roadTest: Driving skills test given by a DMV examiner, scheduled online at wisconsindmv.gov/roadtest.
Wisconsin.restrictions: For the first nine months (extendable until 18), no driving from midnight to 5 a.m. except between home and school or work, and only one passenger besides immediate family or a qualified adult.

Wyoming.agency: Wyoming Department of Transportation (WYDOT), Driver Services
Wyoming.permitTest: Written knowledge exam and vision screening at a driver exam office.
Wyoming.permitDocuments: Apply in person (you can start online at oneWYO) with the required identity documents and a parent or guardian signature if under 18.
Wyoming.driversEd: Not required for the intermediate permit, but anyone under 17 needs an approved driver education course to get full privileges after 6 months on the intermediate permit (otherwise they wait until 17); an approved driver ed program may give the driving skills test.
Wyoming.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, certified by a parent or guardian
Wyoming.roadTest: Driving skills test with WYDOT Driver Services at a local driver exam office, or through an approved driver education program. Apply in person, surrender the learner's permit, bring Real ID documents and the 50-hour certification, and pass a vision screening; a parent or guardian signs.
Wyoming.restrictions: Intermediate permit holders may drive only from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. and may carry no more than one non-family passenger under 18, unless accompanied by a licensed adult 18 or older (written exceptions for work, school, medical, and religious activities).
